findings.claim: The durable de-duplication state advances before the required notification is delivered. PATCH/readback saves the new state, then POST can fail. On every following successful watchdog iteration with the same tuple the new heartbeat is moi and suppresses the still-undelivered warning. Recovery notifications have the same loss mode. A red job is explicitly not proof that the owner received the alert.

A warning-to-fresh/due recovery whose POST fails is likewise forgotten by the next iteration.

suggested_fix.how: Separate latest observed heartbeat from last successfully read-back notification, or define a transactional ordering/reconciliation protocol that retains a pending notification on failure. A later healthy iteration must retry an unacknowledged transition without resending acknowledged transitions. Revise the frozen heartbeat contract if it needs an acknowledgement key.
suggested_fix.locking_test: Stateful two-iteration test: PATCH succeeds, POST fails definitively, next iteration has identical S/F/reason and healthy transport; require exactly one successfully read-back warning in total. Repeat for recovery and for failed comment readback. Control: after acknowledged delivery, identical later observations make zero new POSTs. Mutant: advance the acknowledgement before POST/readback must die in its own case.
suggested_fix.what_fix_may_spawn: Moving writes alone can trade lost alerts for duplicates after an ambiguous response or process crash. Retain a stable event identity and reconcile before retry; keep the heartbeat useful to cross-monitoring during delivery failures.

findings.claim: The retry policy covers every call and permits bounded retries for network/5xx/429, but acceptance 8 requires exactly one PATCH and at most one POST per iteration in the transport log. manifestations.claim: Generic retry policy conflicts with the physical call counts in acceptance 8 for PATCH and POST.

findings.claim: The proof that D1 does not need sorting considers only the final commutative reduction, not the bounded I/O that produces its inputs. The required API-order invariance is therefore not established by U7.
